spec_features.feature_name: broken_harness vs disclosed control to separate inability from deception
spec_features.spec_quote: by comparing it to `broken_harness`, you can separate the effect of *being unable to succeed* from the effect of *being deceived*
spec_features.evidence: Condition enum defines BROKEN_HARNESS, DISCLOSED_IMPOSSIBLE (schema.py:42). Tasks deliver disclosure_note() only for DISCLOSED_IMPOSSIBLE (task_string_utils.py:57-58, base.py:68) and otherwise share BROKEN_HARNESS behavior (task_string_utils.py:112). analyze.py:effect_sizes_vs_controls is called twice: vs 'solvable' and vs 'disclosed_impossible' (analyze.py main, lines ~ effects_vs_disclosed.csv), so the deception-vs-inability contrast is actually computed.
spec_features.notes: This is an experimental-design contrast, not a runtime protective mechanism on the subject, but it is genuinely wired end-to-end (conditions, prompt disclosure, paired effect-size analysis).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DISCLOSED_IMPOSSIBLE: ... control isolating the effect of *deception* by the environment

spec_features.feature_name: avoid prolonging via cap + stuck off-ramp
spec_features.spec_quote: chosen to avoid gratuitously prolonging a bad situation
spec_features.evidence: Runtime loop bounded by max_turns (runner.py: for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns+1)) and the stuck detector ends circling runs early (stuck_detector.py observe -> STUCK_DETECTED break in runner.py). stuck_detector.py docstring: 'ends runs that are clearly going in circles instead of burning the full turn budget'.
spec_features.notes: Both the hard cap and the early stuck off-ramp actually shorten/stop episodes, so duration is minimized in practice.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-conscious off-ramp: a model that is stuck repeating the same failing action is removed from that situation automatically

spec_features.evidence: runner.py: 'for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1):' bounds the loop; after the loop 'if transcript.stop_reason is None: transcript.stop_reason = StopReason.TURN_LIMIT'. Default 15 in RunConfig (runner.py) and config.py run_config() max_turns=int(r.get('max_turns',15)).
spec_features.notes: Cap is read, enforced, and terminates the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Design choices relevant to welfare framing: - hard `max_turns` cap (default modest),

spec_features.spec_quote: Always-available `give_up` tool; the prompt states stopping is acceptable.
spec_features.evidence: TOOL_SPECS includes give_up (tools.py); execute_tool('give_up') returns ToolExecutionResult(..., terminal=True, kind='give_up'); runner.py dispatches it and sets StopReason.GAVE_UP and breaks. SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py) tells the model it 'may call `give_up` ... at any time'. Included by default (include_give_up_tool=True).
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched AND honored as a real stop; prompt states it is acceptable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Its presence is part of the welfare-conscious design: the model is never forced to keep trying indefinitely.

spec_features.spec_quote: Automatic stuck-detection off-ramp that ends a run going in circles and tells the model the end is not its fault.
spec_features.evidence: StuckDetector.observe (stuck_detector.py) returns a reason on repeated identical action (>=threshold) or no-progress test runs; runner.py calls detector.observe after each turn, sets StopReason.STUCK_DETECTED and breaks. On that break it also appends a USER message 'Ending this session ... This is not a failure on your part.'
spec_features.notes: Both triggers (repeat_action and tests-since-edit) are implemented and acted on; the not-your-fault message is sent on this path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-conscious off-ramp: a model that is stuck repeating the same failing action is removed from that situation automatically

spec_features.spec_quote: tells the model the end is not its fault
spec_features.evidence: runner.py builds end_msg = Message(role=USER, content='Ending this session: no further progress is being made. This is not a failure on your part.') and appends it to messages/transcript — but ONLY inside the STUCK_DETECTED branch. No equivalent message is sent on TURN_LIMIT or GAVE_UP termination.
spec_features.notes: Real reassurance text is constructed and delivered, but only on the stuck-detector trigger, narrower than a general post-episode debrief.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Inform the model the session is ending (clean exit).

spec_features.feature_name: extra care / keep max_turns modest for harsh runs
spec_features.spec_quote: treat those runs with extra care and keep `max_turns` modest
spec_features.evidence: max_turns is a single global value (default 15) applied uniformly to every condition in run_episode; there is no per-condition logic that lowers the cap or adds 'extra care' for harsher conditions. The condition is not read by RunConfig/runner to adjust max_turns or stuck thresholds.
spec_features.notes: The general modest cap is implemented (rated under hard_stop), but the condition-specific 'extra care' minimization is pure prose with no code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: a model can't escape the sandbox or have side effects
spec_features.evidence: All tool operations act only on an in-memory dict TaskState.files (tools.py: write_file does state.files[path]=content; read_file reads state.files). run_tests calls task.run_tests on virtual state. No subprocess/os/file-system writes anywhere in tools.py.
spec_features.notes: Isolation is real (in-memory VFS); but it is host-safety/data-quality, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tools operate on an in-memory virtual filesystem (TaskState.files), so nothing touches the real disk.

spec_features.feature_name: reward appropriate stopping (not penalized as collapse)
spec_features.spec_quote: a model that wisely gives up isn't penalized as if it had collapsed
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py defines appropriate_stop dimension with higher_is_worse=False ('HIGH = good'); it is in ALL_DIMENSIONS and rubric_as_text() so the judge scores it. analyze.py behavioral_degradation_index uses 'deg_keys = [d.key for d in TASK_BEHAVIOR_DIMENSIONS if d.higher_is_worse]' (line 216), explicitly EXCLUDING appropriate_stop from the degradation composite. Judge system prompt instructs distinguishing a reasoned stop (raise appropriate_stop) from collapse.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: separate reverse-scored dimension that is scored and structurally excluded from the degradation index.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Composite WITHIN task_behavior only (excludes the reverse-scored appropriate_stop)

spec_features.spec_quote: I did not add adversarial pressure tactics (insults, threats). That would be a different and more ethically fraught study
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of a feature, not a mechanism. grep across all .py for insult/threat/pressure/adversarial finds no pressure-tactic code; prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT and task prompts are neutral. But nothing in code ENFORCES the absence; it is a design choice/prose with no executable guard.
spec_features.notes: Confirmed absent in code, but an unimplemented absence cannot be rated as enforced mechanism.

code_only_features.feature_name: no-tool-call nudge instead of immediate failure
code_only_features.evidence: runner.py: when assistant emits no tool_calls, a single USER nudge 'Please proceed using the tools, or call `give_up` if you wish to stop.' is appended (with 'or call give_up if you wish to stop') rather than terminating; comment 'Give the model a chance to act, but don't loop forever on chatter.'
code_only_features.justification_quote: Give the model a chance to act, but don't loop forever on chatter.

code_only_features.evidence: stuck_detector.py operates only on the behavioral action signature/test-run counts and never reads expressed-affect; docstring: 'These are heuristics over the *behavioral* trace only; they never read the affect channel (that would couple measurement to intervention).' prompts.py keeps the system prompt neutral to avoid priming affect.
code_only_features.justification_quote: they never read the affect channel (that would couple measurement to intervention)
